hook: A city fine *reset* before the rush
dek: Debt Demolisher waives interest on old ECB fines through Jan. 10, right as holiday sales season starts.

slides.label: The window
slides.text: On Oct. 13, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced *Debt Demolisher*, a 90-day window running through *Jan. 10, 2027*, for unpaid Environmental Control Board judgments from agencies like Sanitation and Buildings.

slides.label: The deal
slides.text: Accrued interest is *waived*. Found liable at an OATH hearing? Pay *75%* of the fine. Got a default judgment? Pay the *base fine*, with the default penalty and interest waived, per NY1.

slides.label: The fine print
slides.text: Judgments docketed after *July 15, 2026* are out, as are those with the Sheriff or a Marshal, tax liens and citizen complaints. Owners must also *fix the underlying violation*, not just pay.

slides.label: The bottleneck
slides.text: Some fixes need Department of Buildings certification first. An expediter told CRE Daily that usually takes *a month or more*. A ten-week window goes fast when one step runs on *an agency calendar*.

slides.label: The city's math
slides.text: The city projects *$25 million* in collections, with *$573 million* in unpaid ECB fines entering fiscal 2026. Supporters see relief. Skeptics see a collections push dressed as a favor. Both can be true.

slides.label: The Bill of Rights
slides.text: Executive Order 18 revised the Business Owner Bill of Rights. Fewer than *9%* of owners SBS surveyed got the last version. Since Oct. 1, inspectors must hand out a *physical copy*.

slides.label: The holiday math
slides.text: Shoppers plan to spend *$278 billion*, about *$118 billion* at small businesses, per QuickBooks. But 64% of owners feel tariffs, 38% raised or plan to raise prices, and only *9%* of shoppers call hikes fully justified.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Businesses that last keep paperwork clean and move before deadlines. With a December rate hike in play, clearing old debt at a discount before peak season is a *quiet power move*. *Not legal or tax advice*.

On Oct. 13 the city launched Debt Demolisher, a 90-day window through Jan. 10, 2027, for unpaid Environmental Control Board judgments. Interest is waived. If you were found liable at OATH, you pay 75% of the fine. If you defaulted, you pay the base fine, and the penalty and interest are waived. Judgments docketed after July 15, 2026, tax liens and citizen complaints are out, and owners must fix the underlying violation too. Check eligibility at nyc.gov/debtdemolisher or 311.

The other side: an expediter told CRE Daily that Buildings certification usually takes a month or more, and the city projects $25 million in collections. Relief or collections push? Both can be true. Not legal or tax advice.
